tasks.title: Audit current SQLite schema and document all tables, indexes, and constraints
Choose Postgres hosting provider (e.g. Supabase, Railway, Neon, self-hosted)
Define migration success criteria (zero data loss, all tests green, multi-device smoke test)
Identify SQLite-specific queries or features that need to be rewritten for Postgres
Provision dev/staging Postgres instance
Add Postgres connection string to environment config / secrets manager
Update ORM/query layer to support Postgres dialect (e.g. swap driver, update config)
Provision production Postgres instance and lock down access controls
Write Postgres-compatible schema migration scripts (from SQLite schema audit)
Run migrations against dev Postgres instance and verify schema
Add and validate indexes for common query patterns
Set up a migration version control strategy (e.g. Flyway, Liquibase, or custom)
Write a one-time data migration script to export SQLite data and import into Postgres
Validate row counts and spot-check data integrity after migration
Do a dry-run data migration on staging environment
Rewrite any SQLite-specific raw queries for Postgres compatibility
Update connection pooling settings appropriate for Postgres
Update error handling for Postgres-specific error codes
Run full test suite against Postgres dev instance and fix failures
Write a rollback plan in case production cutover fails
Run final data migration on production instance during low-traffic window
Flip production environment variable to point to Postgres and deploy
Smoke test multi-device use case end-to-end in production
Monitor error rates, query latency, and connection pool health post-cutover
Decommission SQLite file and remove legacy SQLite driver/dependencies

assumptions: The app currently uses an ORM or query builder (not just raw SQL), so dialect-switching is feasible
A staging/dev environment exists or can be stood up quickly
Data volumes are small enough that a one-time migration script (rather than a live dual-write strategy) is sufficient
Multi-device support is the primary driver, so shared network-accessible Postgres is the right end state
There are existing tests that can be run against a different DB backend
questions: Are you using an ORM (e.g. Prisma, SQLAlchemy, Drizzle) or raw SQL? This affects how much query rewriting is needed.
Do you have an existing test suite with meaningful coverage?
What is the approximate data size in SQLite today — bytes, rows, tables?
Do you have a preferred Postgres hosting provider, or is that still open?
Is there a specific deadline tied to the Compass v1 ship date that constrains this migration timeline?
